# PLAN — iteration 2
## Current state assessment
Iteration 1 passed behavior, annotation, verification, and routed timing, but used the same 6 LUTs as the timing-feasible incumbent, so it failed the strict `minimize_luts` objective. Its inlined sequential logic did not improve area.

## Hypothesis
Represent the 8-cycle debounce interval with a 3-bit saturating counter instead of the 4-bit counter, potentially reducing mapped LUT use while preserving the existing behavior.

## Instruction for generator
Keep the top interface and `// @latency 0` annotation, and replace the current 4-bit count representation with a 3-bit count that resets to 0, becomes 1 on a `noisy`/candidate mismatch, increments on matching cycles until 7, then holds at 7. When the prior count is 7 and `noisy` still matches the candidate, update `clean` to the candidate; preserve synchronous active-high reset of candidate, count, and clean. This is a concrete change from iteration 1’s equivalent inline logic; strict acceptance still requires fewer than 6 LUTs and all verification, routed-report, setup, and hold gates to pass.
